paper_title: Distributed cross-learning for equitable federated models — privacy-preserving prediction on data from five California hospitals
prediction_task: Federated clinical prediction (COVID-19, hip arthroplasty, MI) across 5 UC Health centers

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Empirical validation uses logistic regression which is simple and linearly scales. Rationale for distributed file system is undermotivated for 100-variable LR. Need to demonstrate with significantly larger and more complex models.

XGBoost and MLP are still conventional models. Would be more relevant with transformers, CNNs, LSTM. The concept of federated learning is not new, blockchain technology not new — fail to see significant novelty and technical contributions.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified that clinical contribution (privacy-preserving multi-site prediction) is the novelty, not the FL algorithm itself.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Comparison to centralized LR alone is insufficient. Should benchmark against state-of-the-art tree-based algorithms and deep neural networks using the substantial dataset.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added centralized XGBoost and MLP comparisons.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Evaluation should include F1-score, recall, precision, and sensitivity beyond just AUC. Distribution of outcomes and class balance needs clearer presentation.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added full metric panel and class distribution table.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Characteristics of each dataset including demographics and covariates should be clearly outlined in a table.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added comprehensive demographics table per site.

reviewer_strengths.text: Proposed method is promising with prediction performance comparable to centralized modeling. Paper is well-written and organized.
